text:
DeployBot: initiating canary rollout inference-service:v4 -> 20% (strategy=canary) at 2026-03-15T09:10:00Z

Alex: noticed spike of CrashLoopBackOff on inference-rr-2 and inference-rr-4

Priya: tailing logs, looks like OOM on startup repeatedly

Priya: ```
kubectl -n inference logs inference-rr-2
...
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
exit code 137
```

IncidentBot: paging #oncall-alex (reason: deploy error rate exceeded)

Alex: ack, investigating HPA and pod restarts

Maya: HPA scaled from 3 -> 12 when canary traffic hit; pods are bouncing and being evicted

Jason: infra maintenance triggered a node drain on node-9 around 09:08, overlap with rollout

Priya: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep inference-rr`
inference-rr-2   0/1 CrashLoopBackOff   6   4m   10.0.1.45   node-7
inference-rr-4   0/1 CrashLoopBackOff   5   3m   10.0.1.47   node-9

Maya: PDB prevented smooth reschedule; drain caused pods to be repeatedly killed on same node

Jason: root cause hypothesis: new image v4 has increased heap usage + simultaneous node drain + aggressive HPA burst -> OOMs and churn

Alex: customer metrics show 5xx increase for several EU customers; SupportBot created ticket INC-4821

SupportBot: affected: eu-corpA, eu-startupX, eu-merchantZ. Error rate peaked ~18% for /v1/generate between 09:12-09:18 UTC

Priya: propose immediate mitigation: disable model_v4_enabled feature flag (kill-switch)

Alex: flipping model_v4_enabled -> false via admin UI

Alex: model_v4_enabled set to false :white_check_mark:

DeployBot: diverting canary traffic back to stable v3 pool; monitoring

Priya: initiating deployment rollback: `kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/inference --to-revision=3`

DeployBot: rollback to v3 started for deployment inference

Maya: removed scheduled drain on node-9 to stop further churn while rollback completes

Jason: force-deleting crashed pods to let controller create fresh instances on healthy nodes

Jason: `kubectl delete pod inference-rr-2 --grace-period=0 --force -n inference`

Priya: after rollback + pod cleanup, 500 errors fell back to baseline within ~90s

SupportBot: sent customer-facing update; internal status page updated. No data corruption; client retries succeeded.

IncidentBot: severity lowered to SEV-2; monitoring continues

Alex: handing off to Maya for postmortem and timeline (I need to step off)

Maya: taking ownership. Postmortem agenda: (1) avoid scheduling node drains during canary windows or add drain-guard, (2) HPA policy tuning: add cooldown and burst limits, (3) add memory/regression test in CI for JVM images, (4) refine feature-flag kill-switch runbook with steps and verification

Maya: immediate action items assigned: Priya - memory profiling + JVM opt hotfix; Jason - update infra maintenance calendar + implement drain guard; Alex - quick rollback checklist and oncall notes

Alex: posting quick notes to incident channel and linking support tickets

Maya: ETA for postmortem draft 2026-03-16T18:00Z

SupportBot: closing customer incident notice; will reopen if regressions occur

Alex: thanks for the fast work. Good catch on the drain overlap :thumbsup:

DeployBot: rollout aborted, stable v3 serving. Health checks passing.
